subject: Genetics
title: The Cost of Sequencing
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Cost of Sequencing usable.

hook.text: The first human genome cost $2.7 billion to sequence. Today it costs under $200. That's a 13-million-fold drop.

buildup.text: Moore's Law doubles computing power every two years. Sequencing costs dropped faster—doubling every few months.

discovery.text: Next-gen sequencers read millions of fragments simultaneously. Illumina's machines process a genome in hours.

twist.text: Cheap sequencing changed who uses it. It's no longer just research—it's medicine, agriculture, and forensics.

climax.text: At $200, sequencing your genome is cheaper than an MRI. The technology outran even the optimists' predictions.

punchline.text: From $2.7 billion to $200. Nothing in tech dropped faster.

quiz.question: How much does it cost to sequence a human genome today?
